name: Sampait

attributes.attribute: an Irish heroine who defended herself against a man of rank
the man who tried to force Sampait and was killed by her

sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924, 23–25.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sampait is an Irish heroine. Her name appears in some sources as Sempait. Her story comes from the Dindshenchas, the place-lore of early Ireland. She was a farmer and a bard. One day a man of rank, Crechmael, tried to force her while she tended her flock. She refused his demand. The old account records what she did in return. She bound him like a pig meant for slaughter. In that way the herdswoman punished the man who would use her. Ireland kept her name in its place lore. The tale stands as a warning that force met a harsh answer.

okr.objective: Document Sampait, the Irish heroine who resisted assault.
